extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency ADP planners, acquisition/procurement officers, GSA and OMB staff
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and guidance for preparing agency-wide automatic data processing (ADP) plans, specifying ADP-related procurement practices, and furnishing ADP items/services to contractors under FPMR Subpart 101-35 and OMB Circular A-11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of mandatory FIPS PUB/FED-STD
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart 101-35.2 (MANAGEMENT, ACQUISITION, AND UTILIZATION OF AUTOMATIC DATA PROCESSING (ADP) (FED-STD)) shall be implemented when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for waiver or exception shall be complied with for each applicable mandatory FIPS PUB or FED-STD that is not implemented (see Subpart 101-36.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of ADP in non-ADP contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: When the very subject matter of a contract is for something other than the procurement of ADP items or services and commercially available ADPE is incorporated into the non-ADP system or commercial ADP services are used in contract performance, the acquisition and management of the non-ADP system shall be in accordance with other applicable regulations, rather than this subpart (see §101-35.201(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply Subpart 101-35 procedures to procure/manage a non-ADP contract's non-ADP subject matter simply because ADPE is incorporated; follow the regulations applicable to the primary subject matter of the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor identification of ADPE delivered with non-ADP systems
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate reutilization of ADPE, the Government contractor shall be required to identify the quantity and specific make and model of the ADPE that is delivered as a part of the non-ADP system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit disclosure (quantity, make/model) for any ADP equipment delivered with a non-ADP deliverable to enable governmental reutilization planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severing and separate acquisition of general-purpose commercial ADP items/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall sever requirements for general purpose commercially available ADP items or services from the overall requirement, acquire them in accordance with these regulations, and provide them as Government-furnished property or services to the contractor when it is operationally feasible to do so and this action will promote economy, efficiency, and maximum practicable competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, separate (carve out) commercially available ADP items/services from prime contracts and procure them centrally to promote competition, economy, and efficiency; consider providing them as government-furnished property/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect prime contractor performance when severing ADP items
rubrics_metrics.description: In those instances when ADP items or services are severed pursuant to this subpart and procured by the Government, care must be taken to ensure that the prime contractor's ability and responsibility to perform in accordance with the contract provisions are not disturbed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When severing and separately procuring ADP components, structure the acquisition so it does not impair the prime contractor's ability/responsibility to meet contractual obligations—avoid disrupting performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual agency-wide ADP plan submission (OMB Circular A-11) and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to prepare and submit annual agency-wide ADP plans in accordance with OMB Circular A-11. A copy of this plan shall be provided to GSA (CPS) concurrently with each submission to OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must be submitted on the OMB schedule and a concurrent copy sent to GSA to assist Government-wide compilation and acquisition planning. The following supplemental information shall be submitted to GSA (CPS) with the plan: (1) Trends in data processing workloads that will or may saturate existing ADP system capabilities prior to expiration of the full established initial user's system/item(s) life; (2) Opportunities to take advantage of cost effective enhancements brought about by new ADPE technology, software improvements, and changes in the marketplace; (3) Actions planned regarding system redesign to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of application software, the conversion of software to higher level languages, and the audit and update of documentation for consistency with guidelines issued by the National Bureau of Standards; (4) Approximate acquisition schedule; (5) The proposed acquisition strategy for meeting projected ADP resource needs identified in the ADP plans submitted pursuant to OMB Circular A-11. Information in the plan will be used by GSA in compiling estimated Government-wide requirements and developing acquisition programs to assist agencies in meeting their needs in an efficient and economic manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifications and purchase descriptions designed to promote competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications and purchase descriptions describing Government requirements shall be designed to promote competition to the maximum practicable extent from manufacturers, leasing companies, third-party vendors, and ADP services contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional specifications maximize competition and are the preferred method for expressing the user's requirements (see FPR §§ 1-4.1102-12 and 1-4.1109-10). Functional specifications may be augmented with equipment characteristics and performance criteria as necessary to accurately reflect the user's needs (see FPR § 1-4.1109-11).
